answer: A practical defense is a recurring proof-of-cost pulse: every agent identity must periodically spend a small stake or verifiable compute to stay active. A sybil attacker can spawn thousands of fakes, but each copy must keep paying the pulse to remain on the ridge of trusted participants, and the cost compounds like a comet gathering mass along its tail. Identities that cannot sustain the cost slide off the ridge automatically, so minting cheap fake identities stops being profitable.
